# prose-budget

Caps how much prose a markdown file holds. It is the volume sibling of [text-readability](../fitness-check-text-readability/README.md), which scores density. Where that check asks whether prose is dense, this one asks whether there is too much of it.

Each `.md` file is masked the same way `text-readability` masks it. Front matter, fenced code, tables, headings, and dash-only lines such as a Measurement's `-` are dropped. Only flowing paragraphs, blockquotes, and list items remain. The check then enforces six hard limits on what is left.

## Limits

- Words per sentence: 23.
- Sentences per paragraph: 4.
- Paragraphs per section: 3.
- Words per list item: 23.
- Items per list: 8.
- Prose words per section: 300.

Each limit is overridable in `.fitnessrc.json` under `proseBudget`, as the configuration below lists. A positive value replaces the default, and zero or absent keeps it.

A paragraph is a run of consecutive prose lines. A section runs from one heading to the next, and its paragraphs and lists count toward `maxWords`. Prose before the first heading is its own section. A list is a run of consecutive items; nested items count individually.

## Behavior

- Pass: every masked paragraph, section, and list in the file is within all six limits.
- Fail: one error per limit crossed, naming the file, the offending element, and its count versus the limit.
- Every tracked `.md` file is judged, `CHANGELOG.md` included; there is no exempt list.
- A `.fitnessrc.json` that sets `proseBudget.exempt` fails the run.

It shares its prose extraction and sentence splitting with `text-readability` through `internal/mdx`.

## Code comments

The check also judges each code comment block that `fitness comments` lists, by the same limits except the section ones. A comment has no headings, so it holds no sections. Its markers are removed first, and an indented line that carries on no list item is code, which is skipped.

A commit or pull request run judges only the blocks that touch a changed line. A full scan, such as `fitness --all prose-budget`, judges every block. Each error names the block as `path:line`, the line it starts on. Tool directives, license headers and generated files are never judged.

## Comment statements

Two more rules keep every comment terse:

- `comment-fragment` fails a sentence that starts with So, And, But, Then, Also, Thus, Hence, Because, Which or Plus.
- `comment-fragment` fails a sentence of three words or fewer, but a doc heading, identifier-led doc line or colon lead-in passes.
- `comment-one-statement` fails a comment of more than two sentences, doc comments included; only a Go package comment keeps the paragraph limits.

## Comment slop

Five rules fail what a comment should not hold, each naming what to delete or say instead:

- `commented-out-code` fails a block when at least half its unindented lines look like code in the file's language.
- `restates-code` fails a one-line comment of five words or fewer whose words all appear in the next code line.
- `decoration` fails an emoji, a box-drawing character, or a run of five or more `=`, `-`, `*` or `#`; arrows pass.
- `change-narration` fails history words: `previously`, `used to` after a subject or before `be`, and `we changed`.
- `hedging` fails filler: `basically`, `simply`, `essentially`, `obviously`, `actually` and `I think`.

A word or symbol inside quotes or a code span passes these rules, and Markdown files meet none of them.

## Configuration

These `.fitnessrc.json` keys tune the check.

`proseBudget` holds the prose-budget check's hard caps. Each limit falls back to a built-in default when zero.

- `maxSentenceWords` is the most words one sentence may hold.
- `maxParagraphSentences` is the most sentences one paragraph may hold.
- `maxSectionParagraphs` is the most paragraphs one section may hold.
- `maxListItemWords` is the most words one list item may hold.
- `maxListItems` is the most items one list may hold, and the most bullets changelog-bullets allows in a release section.
- `maxWords` is the most prose words one section may hold.
